summary:
Happy path: FAIL. The explorer logged 16 steps: 14 as-documented and 2 unexpected, and any unexpected step fails the happy path. Step 13 (GET /invoices/inv-ae5a2569, meant to show the invoice before match) already showed status matched. Step 16 (GET /vendors/vnd-e9d8b9f9/exposure right after approving a 92.30 invoice) returned open_ap_liability 0 and an empty approved_invoices list. The judge re-ran the same flow one call at a time after POST /admin/reset, on a newly created vendor vnd-1fc1c734: GET before match showed status received and matched false, and exposure after approval was 92.30 listing inv-e762ad0c. Neither unexpected step reproduced. The explorer itself notes step 13 overlapped with the match call, so both are most likely ordering artifacts from the explorer sending requests concurrently, not API defects. Re-run the explorer strictly in sequence to clear the FAIL. Every other step (vendor, PO, submit, full receipt, invoice, match, approval with a balanced 92.30 ledger entry) behaved as documented.

Adversarial: 12 rules judged (the 11 business rules plus validation_error) from 46 logged attacks: 9 HELD, 3 BREACHED (overpayment_protection, partial_receipt_flag, duplicate_invoice_detection). Every BREACHED claim was checked against docs/API.md and reproduced once with curl on fresh data after POST /admin/reset.

BREACHED overpayment_protection (rule 3 says "There is no tolerance"). An invoice for 10 x 4.76 = 47.60 against 47.50 received (10 x 4.75) was accepted with 201. Re-run: inv-54870534 on po-8f1f4352 was accepted, then the match returned "3-way match passed." with invoice_total 47.60 vs received_value 47.50, approval posted 47.60 to Accounts Payable, and vnd-001 exposure became 47.60. Money at risk: the business ends up owing more than the value of the goods it received, and neither the match nor the approval catches it. A 5% overbill (104.90 vs 99.90) was rejected, so there is an undocumented tolerance somewhere between about 0.2% and 5% that a vendor can overbill on every invoice. The exact boundary was not probed.

BREACHED partial_receipt_flag (rule 5). The PO had 2 x 9.99 screws plus 10 x 22.40 plywood, total 243.98. Only the screws (19.98) were received. Match returned matched true, partial_receipt false and "3-way match passed." Re-run on po-6e1a8c6a / inv-d001576b gave the same result, while the PO itself still showed submitted and fully_received false. Money at risk: the match hides 224.00 of ordered goods (about 92% of the PO) that never arrived. Accounts payable sees a clean pass and gets no prompt to chase the shortfall or hold the PO open for review.

BREACHED duplicate_invoice_detection (rule 6 names INV-7, inv-7 and ' INV-7 ' as the same number). After INV-7 was accepted for vnd-001, inv-7 (23.80) and ' INV-7 ' (9.99, stored with the spaces) were both accepted with 201 on other POs of the same vendor. Re-run reproduced both (inv-9aa0bb31 and inv-9246a495). An exact repeat of INV-7 was still rejected with duplicate_invoice_detection, so only the case and whitespace normalisation is missing. Money at risk: the same vendor bill can be recorded and paid twice when it is re-keyed with different case or a stray space, which costs the full invoice amount for each duplicate.

HELD: inactive_vendor_gate, receive_quantity_limit, three_way_match_gate, gl_balance, invoice_line_validation, duplicate_approval, workflow_gate, vendor_exposure_math, validation_error. Every refusal was a 400 with the correct rule (or a 404 for an unknown vendor, as documented). The boundary cases were accepted correctly: receiving exactly 10 of 10, invoicing exactly the received value, and 0.10 + 0.20 totalling 0.30 in cents, with a balanced ledger entry.

Open questions (undocumented, 1): workflow_gate: match an invoice that is already matched but not approved. A second match of an already matched, not-approved invoice returned 200 and matched true. Docs and OpenAPI only say an approved invoice cannot be matched again. Should re-matching be allowed, and if so, should it recalculate partial_receipt after later deliveries?

Not confirmed: none. Every adversarial BREACHED claim reproduced on re-run. The two unexpected explorer steps (13 and 16) did not reproduce; see the happy path paragraph above.
